posts.text: 5 This time the timeline may be accelerated given Tehran's urgent need for economic relief and Trump's lack of appetite for drawn-out talks. Any deal comes down to three issues: the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, and the duration of an enrichment suspension

4 Even after Khamenei's speech, it took nearly two years of negotiations to reach a nuclear deal. The few instances Tehran has compromised since 1979 have required significant pressure and sustained diplomacy in pursuit of a viable objective (not "total surrender")

3 After the US Congress sanctioned Iran's Central Bank in early 2012, Ayatollah Khamenei gave defiant weekly speeches for 18 months. Yet in Sept. 2013, with no prior warning, he abruptly gave a speech calling for “heroic flexibility”, a signal the regime needed to compromise.

2 This doesn't mean the Islamic Republic will soon capitulate--they have long been willing to subject the Iranian people to enormous economic hardship rather than compromise. Yet the public defiance of Islamic Republic officials does not often capture their private reality.

1 Despite Iran's public bluster, the now 19-day US naval blockade is having an impact. A largely insolvent government battling 70% inflation is losing an estimated $450m daily due to a blockade it cannot easily circumvent. That's not sustainable.

Video

To counter the US blockade, Tehran is reportedly considering unconventional tools including mine-carrying dolphins: "Iranian officials said Tehran could use previously unused weapons to attack U.S. warships, from submarines to mine-carrying dolphins."

The US and Iran went from hot war to mutual strangulation in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran trying to choke the global economy and Trump trying to strangle Iran into submission. Neither side is ready to let go. CNN with @OutFrontCNN

Video

Neither the U.S. nor Iran wants to return to war. The broad contours of a deal are visible, but an agreement itself remains distant. Trump and Tehran share the same instinct: never yield to pressure, always punch back. @CNN with @KaitlanCollins
